name: Migro: Copy Posts & Pages Between Staging and Live
author: migro

sections.description:
You changed one post. Why clone the whole site?

Most WordPress migration plugins were made for moving to a new host: export the whole database, overwrite the live site, and hope nothing breaks.

Migro was made for everyday edits.

Copy single posts and pages between staging and live without touching the rest of the live site. Copy exactly what changed, with its images, categories, tags, page details and author, and leave everything else alone.

Made for agencies, publishers, freelancers and editorial teams who work on a staging site.

No database access needed

Many hosts do not let other servers reach their database. Migro does not need it.

Migro connects through WordPress itself, using an Application Password. Copy a pairing code from one site, paste it on the other, and you are done. No database host, no database user, no database password, no firewall changes.

If the database can be reached, Migro still uses it, because it is faster. If not, Migro connects through WordPress and tells you so. Either way, the result is the same.

What Migro does

Migro copies the content you pick from one site to the other. Choose a post or page, press Copy, and Migro brings only that content and what it needs:

  • Post content, excerpts, slugs, statuses, dates, and comment settings
  • The password on password-protected posts and pages
  • Categories and tags, with parent and child categories kept in order
  • Featured images and images inside the content
  • Image alt text, kept the same in the Media Library and in the post
  • Custom fields and other page details
  • Synced patterns and navigation menus the page uses
  • Which page is your home page, blog page and privacy page
  • The author (or the admin who copied it, if that author is not on the other site)
  • Attached PDFs, videos and other files

It works both ways. Copy changes from staging to live, or copy live content back to staging to test and edit it.

See what a copy will do before it does it

Copying to the live site is the moment people hesitate, so Migro shows you first.

Dry Run goes through your selection one item at a time and shows what would change, with the staging and live versions side by side. Nothing is written until you copy for real.

Migro also remembers what was already copied. On the Copy Content screen, every item is marked Changed, New or In sync, and you can filter by each. Items already in sync are skipped, so copying again only moves what really changed. Choose “Replace it, even if in sync” when you want to copy it anyway.

Why Migro exists

Site migration tools solve hosting problems. Migro solves everyday publishing problems.

Most WordPress teams do not want to:

  • clone the live database
  • overwrite content nobody touched
  • stop publishing while a copy runs
  • redo approved edits by hand
  • risk breaking the live site for one article

They just want to put finished content live, safely. Migro is made for exactly that.

Made for staging and live sites

Whether you are an agency managing client sites or a publisher working with editors and reviewers, Migro fits the way you already work.

  • Copy only what you pick. Copy single posts and pages instead of cloning the whole site.
  • Both directions. Copy staging changes to live, or copy live content back to staging.
  • No duplicates. Copying again updates the same post on the other site, even if its slug or ID is different there.
  • A backup every time. Before anything is replaced, Migro saves a backup you can restore with one click.
  • Editors can copy too. Editors can copy approved content without needing Administrator access.
  • No limits. No monthly caps, no slowdowns, no upgrade prompts.

Main features

  • Dry Run: see item by item what a copy would change, staging and live side by side, before anything is written
  • Migro MCP: AI agents like Claude, Codex and Cursor can check your content and run Dry Runs
  • In sync detection: items already copied are marked “In sync” and skipped, instead of being copied again
  • One-code pairing: connect two sites by pasting one code, with no passwords to copy by hand
  • No database access needed: sites connect through WordPress when the database cannot be reached
  • Copy in both directions between WordPress sites
  • Copy again without creating duplicate posts
  • Automatic backups before anything is replaced, kept as long as you choose
  • Migro Health: notices when a site was overwritten by a copy of the other site’s database, and pauses copies until it is fixed
  • Search, filter and sort your content to find what to copy
  • Editor Access setting: administrators choose whether editors can use Migro at all
  • The other site’s page cache is cleared after a copy that changed content
  • Activity log with the result of every item
  • Saved passwords are encrypted
  • Images already on the other site are reused, not uploaded twice
  • Works with local sites, including Local by WP Engine
  • Sign-in through WordPress Application Passwords
  • Direct database connection when available, for speed
  • Available in English, Brazilian Portuguese and Spanish

Page builder detection

Page builders save layouts in a special format that holds addresses tied to one site. Copying them carelessly can break the layout on the other site.

Migro detects content made with Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder, Bricks, Oxygen, Breakdance, WPBakery, Avada and other page builders. The free version tells you before copying and leaves those pages out, so a copy can never quietly break a layout on the other site.

Migro Pro copies Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder, Bricks, Oxygen and Breakdance layouts safely. It fixes the site addresses and images inside them, brings along the templates and global styles they use, and rebuilds their styles.

AI alt text

Migro can write alt text for images that are missing it, using the WordPress 7.0 AI Connector and your own AI account.

Supported providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google Gemini.

Existing alt text is never overwritten. Requests go straight from your WordPress site to the provider using your own API key. Migro never sits in the middle and never sees your key.

Works with AI agents

Migro MCP lets Claude, Codex, Cursor or any AI tool that supports MCP check what changed and run a Dry Run of a copy. It needs WordPress 6.9 or newer and the official MCP Adapter plugin. An agent acts as the WordPress user whose login it uses, with that user’s permissions.

Migro Pro also lets agents copy and restore backups, once an administrator turns it on. An agent must run a Dry Run of the same items before it can copy them, and a backup is always taken.

Made for live sites

  • If it already exists. Choose Replace it (update the existing post in place) or Leave it alone (do not touch the other site’s post).
  • Reliable backups. Saved before anything is replaced and kept for 30 days, or as long as you choose.
  • Activity log. See which items were copied, skipped or failed, with the reason and a way to try again.
  • Safe passwords. The Application Password, and the database password if you use one, are encrypted before they are saved.
  • Local sites. Works with local and mixed setups, with options for tricky local servers.

How Migro compares to site migration plugins

Site migration plugins move a whole WordPress site. Migro copies content changes.

  • Scope. Migration tools clone the full database. Migro copies only what you pick.
  • When. Migration tools are for a one-time move. Migro is for every day.
  • Side effects. Migration tools overwrite the whole site. Migro leaves everything else alone.
  • Direction. Migration tools go one way. Migro copies both ways.
  • Copying again. Importing again creates duplicates. Migro updates the same post in place.
  • Focus. Migration tools are about hosting. Migro is about publishing.

How it works

  1. Install Migro on both sites
  2. Connect staging and live with one pairing code (no database access needed), or enter the details by hand
  3. Pick the posts or pages to copy
  4. Run a Dry Run to see item by item what would change
  5. Press Copy
  6. Check the results
  7. Restore from a backup in one click if needed

No command line needed. WP-CLI is available in Migro Pro for automation.

Migro Pro

Migro Pro adds more content types and tools:

  • Custom content types
  • Advanced Custom Fields (ACF), including repeaters and galleries
  • Yoast SEO data
  • WooCommerce products, variations, coupons and download files
  • WooCommerce tax and shipping settings
  • Full page builder copying
  • Galleries and forms from other plugins inside page builder layouts
  • Scheduled copies
  • WP-CLI support
  • Quick Copy buttons in the editor and the posts list
  • AI-written SEO titles and descriptions

The free version stays fully working, with no copy limits and no nag screens.

External Services

Migro can connect to two kinds of outside services. Both are off by default and are never contacted unless you choose to use them.

1. AI provider for alt text (optional, opt-in, your own account).

If you turn on AI Enhancements on the AI tab and set up a provider through the WordPress 7.0 AI Connector, Migro sends one image (base64-encoded) and a short prompt to your AI provider to write alt text for that image. Supported providers in the free version are Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google Gemini. The request goes straight from your WordPress site to the provider using your API key; Migro never sits in the middle and never sees your key. No request is made unless you ask for alt text, and existing alt text is never overwritten. Each provider’s terms apply to your account:

  • Anthropic: terms https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms ; privacy https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • OpenAI: terms https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use ; privacy https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy
  • Google Gemini: terms https://policies.google.com/terms ; privacy https://policies.google.com/privacy

2. Anonymous usage data to Migro (optional, opt-in, off by default).

After installation Migro asks once whether you want to share anonymous usage data. Nothing is sent unless you choose Yes. If you say no or ignore the question, no data ever leaves your site, and you can change your choice at any time on the Settings page. When turned on, Migro sends anonymous, non-personal information (plugin version, WordPress version, PHP version, site language, free or Pro, and how many copies ran in each direction) to https://migro.dev to help plan what to build next. It never sends post content, URLs, passwords, or personal information.

  • Migro privacy policy: https://migro.dev/privacy
  • Migro terms of service: https://migro.dev/terms
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/migro-content-migrator
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen
  3. Follow the setup wizard to connect your sites
  4. Start copying content!

Server requirements

Install Migro on both sites. Each one needs:

  • WordPress 5.6 or newer and PHP 7.4 or newer.
  • Application Passwords and the REST API turned on. Some security plugins and hosts turn them off.
  • The two sites able to reach each other over the web, with no firewall blocking requests between them.
  • These PHP extensions: sodium, mbstring, zlib and cURL. Most hosts turn them on by default. Sodium protects saved passwords; if your host turned it off, ask them to turn it on.
  • PDO MySQL, only if you connect the sites through their databases. Without database access, Migro connects through the WordPress REST API instead.

If something is missing, the Health tab on the Migro screen names the problems it can detect, such as a missing sodium extension or a site it cannot reach.
sections.faq:
How is Migro different from Duplicator or All-in-One WP Migration?

Those are site migration tools, made for moving a whole WordPress site from one host to another, all at once. Migro is a content copy tool, made for the everyday job of copying single posts from staging to live while leaving the rest of the live site alone. Different problem, different product.

Do I need to install Migro on both sites?

Yes. Migro needs to be active on both sites.

Do I need access to my database?

No. Since version 2.7, Migro connects through WordPress using an Application Password, so it works on hosts that block outside database access. If the database can be reached, Migro uses it for speed. Settings shows which connection is in use.

Can content go both ways?

Yes. You can copy live content back to staging just as easily as copying staging drafts to live.

What happens to images that already exist on the other site?

Migro checks each image. If the exact same file is already in the other site’s Media Library, Migro uses it instead of uploading a second copy.

Will copying a post change its URL on the other site?

No. Migro keeps the original slug. The URL on the other site matches unless the two sites use different permalink settings.

What’s the difference between Replace it and Leave it alone?

Replace it updates the existing post in place: same post ID, same URL, new content. Leave it alone keeps an existing post on the other site untouched. You choose each time you copy.

What if I copy something by mistake?

Every copy that replaces existing content saves a backup first. The Backups page lets you restore the previous version with one click. Backups are kept for 30 days by default, and Settings lets you change that.

Does the AI alt text feature cost anything?

Migro’s AI feature uses the WordPress 7.0 AI Connector. You bring your own API key (Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google Gemini) and pay your provider directly. Migro never charges you for AI, never sits in the middle, and never sees your key. Alt text it writes is saved, so copying the same content again does not ask the provider again. Existing alt text is never overwritten.

Can Editors copy content, or only Admins?

Editors can copy, and that is the default. For agencies, it lets a client copy their own approved drafts without admin access. Settings, pairing and backups stay administrator-only either way. If you do not want that, the Editor Access setting hides Migro from everyone except administrators. The administrator decides who copies.

Are there any usage limits?

No. Migro is unlimited. There is no monthly cap and no nag screen. The Pro version adds features (custom content types, ACF, Yoast, WooCommerce, scheduling, WP-CLI), not volume.

Does Migro work with multisite?

Migro is made for single sites. Multisite is not supported yet.

Does Migro copy users?

No. User accounts are not copied. If a post’s author is not on the other site, the post is given to the admin who ran the copy.

Is my database password stored securely?

Yes. If you give Migro a database password, it is encrypted before it is saved, and so is the Application Password. Neither is saved or sent as plain text. You can also skip the database entirely: Migro works without it.

Can I use Migro with a staging site on a different server?

Yes. All you need is an administrator account on the other site and an Application Password from it. Database details are optional. Migro also works with local setups such as Local by WP Engine.

Can I see what a copy will change before running it?

Yes. Dry Run goes through your selection one item at a time and shows what would change, with the two versions side by side. Nothing is written to the other site during a Dry Run.

Will copying again overwrite content that has not changed?

No. Migro remembers what was already copied. Items that are the same on both sites are marked “In sync” and skipped, so copying again only moves what really changed. Choose “Replace it, even if in sync” if you want to copy it anyway.

How do I connect two Local by WP Engine (LocalWP) sites?

Copy the pairing code from one site and paste it on the other. That is all: the sites connect through WordPress, with no database settings. To make large copies faster, you can also give Migro the database. LocalWP does not show a database password, and where the database lives depends on your operating system. On macOS and Linux, LocalWP serves MySQL over a Unix socket: open the site’s Database tab in LocalWP and use the socket path shown there as the database host. On Windows, LocalWP serves MySQL over TCP on a per-site port: open the other site in LocalWP, go to the Database tab, note the Port (a five-digit number such as 10017), and enter the host as localhost:10017, using your own port. If the connection is refused, try 127.0.0.1:10017 instead.

What if a copy fails halfway through?

Each item is copied on its own. If one fails, the others keep going. The Activity page shows which items were copied, which were skipped, and which failed, with the reason and a way to try again.

Does Migro copy WooCommerce products?

Yes, with Migro Pro. Products and all their variations are copied with prices, attributes, images and download files, along with coupons and the store’s tax and shipping settings. Stock, sales and reviews stay as they are on each site, so a copy never undoes a real sale.

Does Migro copy WooCommerce orders?

No. Orders, refunds and subscriptions belong to the site that took them, so Migro never copies them, even if you pick one by mistake.

Does Migro work with page builders?

The free version detects page builder content (Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder, Bricks, Oxygen, Breakdance, WPBakery, Avada and others) and leaves those pages out, because page builders save layouts with addresses tied to one site, which break on another site without special care. Migro Pro copies Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder, Bricks, Oxygen, Breakdance and WPBakery layouts safely.

Is Migro translated into other languages?

Yes. English, Brazilian Portuguese (pt_BR) and Spanish (es_ES) are included. The non-English translations started as machine translations and get better with help from the community.

Does Migro collect any usage data?

Only if you say yes. After installation Migro asks once whether you want to share anonymous usage data. Nothing is sent unless you choose “Yes”. If you say no or ignore the question, no data ever leaves your site, and you can change your choice at any time on the Settings page. When turned on, Migro sends anonymous, non-personal information such as the plugin version, WordPress and PHP versions, and how many copies ran. It never sends post content, URLs, passwords, or personal information.

What’s the minimum WordPress version required?

WordPress 5.6. That is the version that added Application Passwords, which Migro uses to sign in to the other site.

  • Compatibility test and preparation for WordPress 7.1.
  • General reliability and maintenance improvements.

2.5.0 – 2026-07-18

  • Large deployments are now far more resilient: work automatically splits across requests and resumes where it left off, so big batches no longer fail on server time limits, and the progress bar tracks the whole deployment instead of resetting on every batch.
  • Only one deployment runs at a time. A deployment started while another is in progress is refused with a clear message instead of the two interfering with each other.
  • One pre-migration backup is created per deployment instead of one per batch, and restores are safer: content is swapped in a single database transaction.
  • Large media files now transfer as streams, greatly reducing memory use, and repeat deployments skip re-downloading media that has not changed.
  • Faster deployments on media-heavy sites: database writes are batched and media lookups no longer scan the whole library for every image.
  • When a media file no longer exists on the source site, Migro now recovers it from the destination’s own media library when possible, and the results list names exactly which files could not be migrated and why.
  • Front page, posts page, and privacy policy page settings now carry over to the destination when those pages are part of the deployment.
  • Custom field values are copied exactly, fixing rare cases where backslashes were stripped from page builder data and custom fields.
  • Post titles containing emoji no longer cause remote log entries to fail silently.
  • Background maintenance no longer runs during admin page loads, making the dashboard snappier.
  • More accurate AI retry behavior: retry hints given in minutes are now honored correctly, and permanent provider errors are no longer retried as if they were temporary.
  • AI timeout handling no longer shortens the available execution time on hosts configured with longer or unlimited limits.
  • Page builder pre-migration check made consistent with migration behavior.
  • Security hardening for data imported from the paired site.
  • General stability improvements and updated translations.

2.4.1 – 2026-07-10

  • Deployment results now show the exact reason when a media file fails to upload to the remote site.
  • More reliable AI alt-text generation: longer provider timeouts for large images, automatic retry when the provider is temporarily rate-limited or overloaded, and provider errors are now reported instead of silently dropped.
  • Security hardening for remote requests, background polling, and database queries.
  • Refreshed user-facing copy and updated translations.
  • General stability improvements.

2.4.0 – 2026-05-29

  • New AI Enhancements tab with optional AI alt-text generation for images missing alt, powered by your WordPress 7.0 AI Connector (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini). Existing alt text is never overwritten, and responses are cached locally so re-migrating the same content does not re-call the provider.
  • When multiple AI providers are configured, each AI-powered feature can be routed to a specific provider.
  • New Alt Text Sync keeps inline alt in post content aligned with the Media Library during migration, with skip and overwrite options for existing values.
  • PDFs, videos, and other attached media referenced by your posts now migrate automatically alongside featured images.
  • Improved deduplication for large images prevents duplicate uploads of scaled variants.
  • More accurate progress reporting during long AI-assisted migrations, so the bar no longer appears stuck.
  • Batch result cards now reveal the full per-item operation summary behind a View details toggle.
  • Settings page self-heals previously saved empty values, and Passive Mode no longer locks on for production sites running on local domains.
  • Refreshed Quick Guide covering AI Enhancements, scheduled migrations, and WP-CLI.
  • General stability improvements, translation updates, and security hardening.

2.3.4

  • Fully tested on WordPress 7.0

2.3.3

  • Improved post parent remapping to preserve hierarchical relationships accurately.
  • Normalized database draft date handling for modern MySQL strict mode environments.
  • Corrected documentation and setup flow to clarify that the Free tier has unlimited migrations.

short_description: You changed one post. Why clone the whole site? Migro copies single posts and pages between staging and live. No database access needed.
description:
You changed one post. Why clone the whole site?

Most WordPress migration plugins were made for moving to a new host: export the whole database, overwrite the live site, and hope nothing breaks.

Migro was made for everyday edits.

Copy single posts and pages between staging and live without touching the rest of the live site. Copy exactly what changed, with its images, categories, tags, page details and author, and leave everything else alone.

Made for agencies, publishers, freelancers and editorial teams who work on a staging site.

No database access needed

Many hosts do not let other servers reach their database. Migro does not need it.

Migro connects through WordPress itself, using an Application Password. Copy a pairing code from one site, paste it on the other, and you are done. No database host, no database user, no database password, no firewall changes.

If the database can be reached, Migro still uses it, because it is faster. If not, Migro connects through WordPress and tells you so. Either way, the result is the same.

What Migro does

Migro copies the content you pick from one site to the other. Choose a post or page, press Copy, and Migro brings only that content and what it needs:

  • Post content, excerpts, slugs, statuses, dates, and comment settings
  • The password on password-protected posts and pages
  • Categories and tags, with parent and child categories kept in order
  • Featured images and images inside the content
  • Image alt text, kept the same in the Media Library and in the post
  • Custom fields and other page details
  • Synced patterns and navigation menus the page uses
  • Which page is your home page, blog page and privacy page
  • The author (or the admin who copied it, if that author is not on the other site)
  • Attached PDFs, videos and other files

It works both ways. Copy changes from staging to live, or copy live content back to staging to test and edit it.

See what a copy will do before it does it

Copying to the live site is the moment people hesitate, so Migro shows you first.

Dry Run goes through your selection one item at a time and shows what would change, with the staging and live versions side by side. Nothing is written until you copy for real.

Migro also remembers what was already copied. On the Copy Content screen, every item is marked Changed, New or In sync, and you can filter by each. Items already in sync are skipped, so copying again only moves what really changed. Choose “Replace it, even if in sync” when you want to copy it anyway.

Why Migro exists

Site migration tools solve hosting problems. Migro solves everyday publishing problems.

Most WordPress teams do not want to:

  • clone the live database
  • overwrite content nobody touched
  • stop publishing while a copy runs
  • redo approved edits by hand
  • risk breaking the live site for one article

They just want to put finished content live, safely. Migro is made for exactly that.

Made for staging and live sites

Whether you are an agency managing client sites or a publisher working with editors and reviewers, Migro fits the way you already work.

  • Copy only what you pick. Copy single posts and pages instead of cloning the whole site.
  • Both directions. Copy staging changes to live, or copy live content back to staging.
  • No duplicates. Copying again updates the same post on the other site, even if its slug or ID is different there.
  • A backup every time. Before anything is replaced, Migro saves a backup you can restore with one click.
  • Editors can copy too. Editors can copy approved content without needing Administrator access.
  • No limits. No monthly caps, no slowdowns, no upgrade prompts.

Main features

  • Dry Run: see item by item what a copy would change, staging and live side by side, before anything is written
  • Migro MCP: AI agents like Claude, Codex and Cursor can check your content and run Dry Runs
  • In sync detection: items already copied are marked “In sync” and skipped, instead of being copied again
  • One-code pairing: connect two sites by pasting one code, with no passwords to copy by hand
  • No database access needed: sites connect through WordPress when the database cannot be reached
  • Copy in both directions between WordPress sites
  • Copy again without creating duplicate posts
  • Automatic backups before anything is replaced, kept as long as you choose
  • Migro Health: notices when a site was overwritten by a copy of the other site’s database, and pauses copies until it is fixed
  • Search, filter and sort your content to find what to copy
  • Editor Access setting: administrators choose whether editors can use Migro at all
  • The other site’s page cache is cleared after a copy that changed content
  • Activity log with the result of every item
  • Saved passwords are encrypted
  • Images already on the other site are reused, not uploaded twice
  • Works with local sites, including Local by WP Engine
  • Sign-in through WordPress Application Passwords
  • Direct database connection when available, for speed
  • Available in English, Brazilian Portuguese and Spanish

Page builder detection

Page builders save layouts in a special format that holds addresses tied to one site. Copying them carelessly can break the layout on the other site.

Migro detects content made with Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder, Bricks, Oxygen, Breakdance, WPBakery, Avada and other page builders. The free version tells you before copying and leaves those pages out, so a copy can never quietly break a layout on the other site.

Migro Pro copies Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder, Bricks, Oxygen and Breakdance layouts safely. It fixes the site addresses and images inside them, brings along the templates and global styles they use, and rebuilds their styles.

AI alt text

Migro can write alt text for images that are missing it, using the WordPress 7.0 AI Connector and your own AI account.

Supported providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google Gemini.

Existing alt text is never overwritten. Requests go straight from your WordPress site to the provider using your own API key. Migro never sits in the middle and never sees your key.

Works with AI agents

Migro MCP lets Claude, Codex, Cursor or any AI tool that supports MCP check what changed and run a Dry Run of a copy. It needs WordPress 6.9 or newer and the official MCP Adapter plugin. An agent acts as the WordPress user whose login it uses, with that user’s permissions.

Migro Pro also lets agents copy and restore backups, once an administrator turns it on. An agent must run a Dry Run of the same items before it can copy them, and a backup is always taken.

Made for live sites

  • If it already exists. Choose Replace it (update the existing post in place) or Leave it alone (do not touch the other site’s post).
  • Reliable backups. Saved before anything is replaced and kept for 30 days, or as long as you choose.
  • Activity log. See which items were copied, skipped or failed, with the reason and a way to try again.
  • Safe passwords. The Application Password, and the database password if you use one, are encrypted before they are saved.
  • Local sites. Works with local and mixed setups, with options for tricky local servers.

How Migro compares to site migration plugins

Site migration plugins move a whole WordPress site. Migro copies content changes.

  • Scope. Migration tools clone the full database. Migro copies only what you pick.
  • When. Migration tools are for a one-time move. Migro is for every day.
  • Side effects. Migration tools overwrite the whole site. Migro leaves everything else alone.
  • Direction. Migration tools go one way. Migro copies both ways.
  • Copying again. Importing again creates duplicates. Migro updates the same post in place.
  • Focus. Migration tools are about hosting. Migro is about publishing.

How it works

  1. Install Migro on both sites
  2. Connect staging and live with one pairing code (no database access needed), or enter the details by hand
  3. Pick the posts or pages to copy
  4. Run a Dry Run to see item by item what would change
  5. Press Copy
  6. Check the results
  7. Restore from a backup in one click if needed

No command line needed. WP-CLI is available in Migro Pro for automation.

Migro Pro

Migro Pro adds more content types and tools:

  • Custom content types
  • Advanced Custom Fields (ACF), including repeaters and galleries
  • Yoast SEO data
  • WooCommerce products, variations, coupons and download files
  • WooCommerce tax and shipping settings
  • Full page builder copying
  • Galleries and forms from other plugins inside page builder layouts
  • Scheduled copies
  • WP-CLI support
  • Quick Copy buttons in the editor and the posts list
  • AI-written SEO titles and descriptions

The free version stays fully working, with no copy limits and no nag screens.

External Services

Migro can connect to two kinds of outside services. Both are off by default and are never contacted unless you choose to use them.

1. AI provider for alt text (optional, opt-in, your own account).

If you turn on AI Enhancements on the AI tab and set up a provider through the WordPress 7.0 AI Connector, Migro sends one image (base64-encoded) and a short prompt to your AI provider to write alt text for that image. Supported providers in the free version are Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google Gemini. The request goes straight from your WordPress site to the provider using your API key; Migro never sits in the middle and never sees your key. No request is made unless you ask for alt text, and existing alt text is never overwritten. Each provider’s terms apply to your account:

  • Anthropic: terms https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms ; privacy https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • OpenAI: terms https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use ; privacy https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy
  • Google Gemini: terms https://policies.google.com/terms ; privacy https://policies.google.com/privacy

2. Anonymous usage data to Migro (optional, opt-in, off by default).

After installation Migro asks once whether you want to share anonymous usage data. Nothing is sent unless you choose Yes. If you say no or ignore the question, no data ever leaves your site, and you can change your choice at any time on the Settings page. When turned on, Migro sends anonymous, non-personal information (plugin version, WordPress version, PHP version, site language, free or Pro, and how many copies ran in each direction) to https://migro.dev to help plan what to build next. It never sends post content, URLs, passwords, or personal information.

  • Migro privacy policy: https://migro.dev/privacy
  • Migro terms of service: https://migro.dev/terms

upgrade_notice.2.8.0: Copies run more than twice as fast, images copy more reliably (galleries, CDNs, cloned sites), and accessibility is improved across the whole plugin. Pro adds WPBakery, ACF link fields and Gravity Forms.
upgrade_notice.2.7.9.1: A small recovery fix. Migro Health now shows the one real cause and helps you recover after wp-config.php security keys change.
upgrade_notice.2.7.9: Fixes migrations over the REST API that could hang on some sites. Update recommended.
upgrade_notice.2.7.8: Several security improvements, and Settings now shows whether the database connection is encrypted.
upgrade_notice.2.7.7: Replaced images now copy even under the same file name, and backups are made only when something changes.
upgrade_notice.2.7.6: A redesigned Batch Migration screen shows what changed, what is new and what is already in sync.
upgrade_notice.2.7.5: Pairing codes are now one-time, with stronger protections between paired sites.
upgrade_notice.2.7.4: Synced patterns, menus, Query Loops and post authors now keep the right content on the destination.
upgrade_notice.2.7.3: Keeps every value of a custom field that holds several, and skips posts whose plugin data cannot be copied safely yet.
upgrade_notice.2.7.2: Fixes plugin settings that could become unreadable after a deployment.
upgrade_notice.2.7.1: Find content faster: search, filter and sort the Batch content list.
upgrade_notice.2.7.0: No database access needed: sites now pair through WordPress itself, so hosts that block outside database access work too.
upgrade_notice.2.6.8: Adds SpeedyCache to the page caches Migro clears on the destination after a deployment, so visitors see the change straight away.
upgrade_notice.2.6.7: Fixes a page losing its place in the page tree when it is deployed. Parent pages are now deployed before their children, and Migro warns before deploying a page whose parent is on neither site.
upgrade_notice.2.6.6: Connection problems are now explained in plain language, with a short list of what to check and the technical detail kept separate. Also repairs a site whose stored credentials could not be read after its security keys changed.
upgrade_notice.2.6.5: Security release. Values from a paired site are now escaped everywhere in the admin, and media stored outside the uploads folder is refused. Updating is recommended.
upgrade_notice.2.6.4: Fixes database errors and a PHP notice that could appear on a newly installed site before setup was finished. Batch deployments are faster and the Batch Size setting now works. Updating is recommended.
upgrade_notice.2.6.3: Security hardening of the admin pages. Deployments now clear the destination page cache when content has changed. Updating is recommended.
upgrade_notice.2.6.2: Security fix: post titles and server messages are now escaped everywhere in the admin, so content from a paired site cannot run scripts in your browser. Updating is recommended.
upgrade_notice.2.6.1: The content list is no longer capped at 200 items, and large selections are no longer silently truncated, so Dry Run and sync checks now cover everything you picked. Migrated media keeps its original year/month folder on the destination. A new Editor Access setting restricts Migro to administrators.
upgrade_notice.2.6.0: Deployments are now smarter with built-in sync detection. Migro automatically tracks matching content and skips identical items to make migrations faster and safer. Use Dry Run to preview exact diffs before deploying, or enable "Re-migrate everything" to force a fresh overwrite.
upgrade_notice.2.5.5: Pairing now works on Windows and between a local development site and a live server. Deleting the plugin removes its settings, logs, and stored credentials.
upgrade_notice.2.5.4: Connecting two sites now takes one pasted code instead of eight fields: generate it on one environment, paste it on the other, and both sides configure themselves.
upgrade_notice.2.5.3: Reliability release: improved media handling during migrations and general maintenance improvements.
upgrade_notice.2.5.2: Adds Migro Health: it detects when a site has been overwritten by a database copy from its paired environment, pauses deployments so live content cannot be damaged, and repairs the configuration in one click.
upgrade_notice.2.5.1: Maintenance release: compatibility with WordPress 7.1 and general reliability improvements.
upgrade_notice.2.5.0: Major reliability release: large deployments split and resume automatically, media transfers use far less memory, missing media can be recovered from the destination library, and front page, posts page, and privacy policy settings now carry over. Includes security hardening.
